intent.raw_query: Portugal Algarve, $2200, beach holiday with wine tasting, September 2026 from London

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning coastlines along the cliffside trail connecting Praia da Marinha to Benagil. Descend to hidden grottos, golden coves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters for a swim. The dramatic limestone rock formations make this an unmissable beach experience.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the world's most beautiful sea caves, accessible only by water. A guided kayak tour takes you through hidden sea arches, natural tunnels, and secluded beaches inaccessible by foot. An unforgettable blend of adventure and natural beauty.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour
experiences.description: Visit local Algarvian wineries in the Lagos and Portimão hinterland, sampling indigenous grape varieties like Negra Mole and Crato Branco. Enjoy guided cellar tours, barrel tastings, and food pairings with regional cheeses and charcuterie. A wonderful way to discover the lesser-known wines of southern Portugal.

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Sunset Boat Tour
experiences.description: Cruise through the stunning Ria Formosa lagoon system, a protected natural park of tidal channels, barrier islands, and rich birdlife. Stop at the pristine Ilha Deserta for a swim and fresh seafood lunch. End the tour with a breathtaking Atlantic sunset over the lagoon.

experiences.name: Sagres Sunset & Ponta de Sagres Fortress Visit
experiences.description: Journey to the dramatic southwestern tip of Europe at Cabo de São Vicente and the historic Sagres Fortress, where Henry the Navigator once planned his great voyages of discovery. Watch the sun dip into the Atlantic from the windswept cliffs, then enjoy local wine and petiscos at a nearby tavern in Sagres village.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Faro Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort (approx. 30–45 min by bus/shuttle). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with the resort area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely stroll along the nearest beachfront to get your bearings. Explore the local promenade, pick up snacks and drinks from a nearby supermarket (Lidl or Pingo Doce) to stock up on budget essentials.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed first dinner at a local tasca (traditional Portuguese tavern) near the resort. Try the house grilled fish or piri-piri chicken with a glass of local Alentejo wine.

meals.breakfast: Skipped (in-flight or grab a pastel de nata from airport café)
meals.lunch: Quick bite at airport or grab takeaway sandwich near resort on arrival
meals.dinner: Local tasca near resort — grilled sardines or chicken piri-piri with house wine (~€10–14/person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light. Buy a reusable water bottle and sunscreen at the supermarket — essential budget savers. Pick up a local SIM card at the airport for cheap data.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning swim and sunrise walk on the beachfront directly accessible from the resort. Enjoy the quieter September crowds. Explore the rock formations and sea caves along the shoreline on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby local beach market or fish market if available. Spend the afternoon at the beach — September water is still warm (around 22–24°C). Pack a picnic lunch from the supermarket.
day_by_day.evening: Head into the nearest town center for a casual evening. Visit a local wine bar and try a glass of Algarve regional wine or Vinho Verde. Walk the old town streets and enjoy the atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Café near resort — galão (Portuguese latte) and pastel de nata (~€2–3)
meals.lunch: Supermarket picnic on the beach — local cheese, bread, olives, fruit (~€5–7)
meals.dinner: Town center restaurant — cataplana de marisco (seafood stew) shared between two (~€12–15/person)

day_by_day.notes: September is ideal — crowds thin out post-August but weather remains excellent. Check if the resort offers free beach equipment (umbrellas/chairs).

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus to Albufeira (one of Algarve's most iconic towns). Explore the old town, the fishermen's beach (Praia dos Pescadores), and the historic center with its whitewashed buildings and cobbled streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at Praia da Oura or Praia de Albufeira — stunning golden sand beaches. Swim, sunbathe, and explore the sea caves accessible by foot at low tide. Grab a cheap gelato from a beachside kiosk.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Albufeira for dinner. Try a local cervejaria (beer hall/seafood restaurant) on the strip. Order grilled sea bream (dourada) with salad and local beer.

meals.breakfast: Resort or local café — toast with butter and jam + coffee (~€2–4)
meals.lunch: Snack kiosk on Albufeira beach — bifana sandwich or tosta mista (~€3–5)
meals.dinner: Cervejaria in Albufeira — grilled fish, salad, bread, and local beer (~€13–16/person)

day_by_day.notes: Local bus from most Algarve towns is very affordable (~€2–4 each way). Download the Rede Expressos or Vamus app for bus schedules. Return bus runs until late evening.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at the resort beach — early swim before the sun gets intense. Practice snorkeling if you brought or can rent gear cheaply nearby. Explore rock pools along the shoreline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local quinta (wine estate) or cooperative winery in the Algarve region for a budget wine tasting. Many offer tastings for €5–10 including 3–4 wines and local cheese pairings. Look for Adega do Cantor or local cooperative wineries.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort area. Cook a simple dinner using ingredients from the local market — fresh local produce, olives, cured meats, and a bottle of regional wine from the supermarket (~€4–6 for a good bottle).

meals.breakfast: Local padaria (bakery) — fresh bread rolls, butter, coffee (~€2–3)
meals.lunch: At the winery — included cheese and charcuterie board with tasting (~€5–10)
meals.dinner: Self-catered at resort — Portuguese charcuterie board with local wine (~€8–10 total)

day_by_day.notes: Wine tasting tip: Algarve produces underrated reds and whites. Look for Vida Nova winery (owned by Cliff Richard) or smaller cooperative wineries for the most authentic and affordable experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Lagos — one of Algarve's most beautiful coastal towns. Take the regional train or bus. Explore the historic town walls, Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos), and the charming old town streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Ponta da Piedade — dramatic golden limestone cliffs and sea caves. This is one of the most breathtaking free sights in all of Portugal. Hike the cliff-top trails and peer down at the turquoise water below.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Lagos town center. Find a local restaurant off the main tourist strip for better value. Try açorda de marisco (seafood bread soup) or grilled tuna steak with local wine.

meals.breakfast: Café in Lagos after arrival — coffee and pastel de nata (~€2–3)
meals.lunch: Takeaway prego roll (beef sandwich) or bifana from a local snack bar in Lagos (~€3–5)
meals.dinner: Lagos restaurant off the main square — tuna steak or seafood açorda with wine (~€12–15/person)

day_by_day.notes: Train from Faro to Lagos costs ~€7–9 one way and takes about 1.5 hours — scenic and budget-friendly. Ponta da Piedade is free to visit on foot. Wear comfortable shoes for cliff walks.

day_by_day.morning: Relax morning at the resort. Sleep in, enjoy a slow breakfast, and spend time reading or journaling on the beach. This is a recovery day — budget travel can be tiring!
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the immediate local area on foot — find a hidden cove or quieter beach section away from resort crowds. Look for local artisan shops or a weekly market if one is running nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset wine session on the beach or resort terrace. Buy a bottle of local Algarve rosé or white wine from the supermarket and enjoy with local olives and bread. Watch the famous Algarve golden sunset.

meals.breakfast: Resort café or local bakery — full Portuguese breakfast (eggs, toast, juice, coffee) (~€4–6)
meals.lunch: Light supermarket picnic on the beach (~€5–6)
meals.dinner: Local restaurant near resort — piri-piri chicken or bacalhau (salt cod) with potatoes (~€10–13/person)

day_by_day.notes: Bacalhau (salt cod) is Portugal's national dish with over 365 recipes — try a different preparation each time you see it on a menu. September sunsets in Algarve are spectacular — don't miss them.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Silves — Algarve's ancient Moorish capital. Take a bus or train. Visit the impressive red sandstone Silves Castle (€3–4 entry) with panoramic views over the surrounding hills and orange groves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Silves Cathedral (Igreja da Sé) and the charming riverside town. Walk along the Arade River. Visit the local market if running. Browse the small craft and produce stalls for affordable souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Wine tasting at a local Silves area winery or wine shop — the inland Algarve produces excellent wines away from tourist prices. Try Quinta dos Vales or similar estate. Return to resort for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Café in Silves after arrival — galão and pastry (~€2–3)
meals.lunch: Silves local restaurant — pork secretos (Iberian pork) with local wine (~€10–12/person)
meals.dinner: Resort area tasca — simple grilled fish with vegetables and local table wine (~€10–12/person)

day_by_day.notes: Silves is inland and cooler than the coast — great for a change of scenery. The castle is genuinely impressive and very affordable. Train to Silves from Faro costs ~€5–7.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning beach walk to collect shells or watch local fishermen bring in their morning catch. Visit a local fish market if nearby — fascinating and free to browse. Chat with vendors for a genuine local experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a kayak or paddleboard from a local beach rental shop (typically €10–15/hour in September, cheaper than peak season). Paddle along the coastline and explore sea caves from the water.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost local event — check town noticeboards or tourist office for fado performances, local festivals, or community events happening in September. Algarve often has end-of-summer cultural events.

meals.breakfast: Local café — coffee, fresh orange juice, and toast with local honey (~€3–4)
meals.lunch: Beachside kiosk or snack bar — fresh grilled sardine sandwich or tosta (~€4–6)
meals.dinner: Local restaurant — arroz de lingueirão (razor clam rice) or açorda (~€11–14/person)

day_by_day.notes: Kayak rentals are significantly cheaper in September than July/August. Always wear a life jacket and check sea conditions before paddling near caves. Ask rental shops about guided cave tours for minimal extra cost.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente — the southwestern tip of Europe. Take a bus from Lagos. Visit the dramatic cliffs of Cabo de São Vicente (free to walk, small lighthouse museum ~€3). Feel the raw Atlantic wind.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Sagres Fortress (Fortaleza de Sagres, ~€3 entry) — historically significant as the base of Prince Henry the Navigator's school of navigation. Walk the windswept promontory and enjoy stunning ocean views.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Sagres village before catching the return bus. Sagres has excellent fresh seafood at reasonable prices due to its fishing heritage. Try percebes (barnacles) or fresh grilled fish.

meals.breakfast: Pack breakfast from supermarket for the bus journey — yogurt, fruit, pastry (~€3–4)
meals.lunch: Sagres snack bar or café near the fortress — soup and sandwich (~€5–7)
meals.dinner: Sagres village restaurant — fresh grilled fish platter with local wine (~€13–16/person)

day_by_day.notes: Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente are among the most dramatic free landscapes in Europe. Wind can be strong even in September — bring a light jacket. Bus connections back to resort area run via Lagos.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at the resort beach. This is a perfect day for swimming, reading, and enjoying the late-season sunshine. September water temperatures are at their annual warmest — perfect for extended swims.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local wine cooperative for a deeper wine tasting experience. The Algarve Wine Route (Rota dos Vinhos do Algarve) includes several affordable stops. Focus on trying local Negra Mole grape variety — unique to the region.
day_by_day.evening: Self-catered romantic beach picnic or terrace dinner. Buy the best local wine you've tasted during the trip from a supermarket, pair with local charcuterie, cheese, and fresh bread. Watch the stars — light pollution is low in Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Local padaria — fresh croissant, coffee, fresh-squeezed orange juice (~€3–4)
meals.lunch: At the winery — tasting with food pairing included (~€8–12)
meals.dinner: Self-catered beach picnic — local wine, presunto (cured ham), queijo da serra (cheese), crusty bread (~€10–12 total)

day_by_day.notes: The Algarve Wine Route is less well-known than Douro or Alentejo but offers authentic experiences at lower prices. Ask at the local tourist office for the most current cooperative winery recommendations.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Faro — the Algarve capital. Explore the historic walled old town (Cidade Velha), the cathedral (Sé de Faro) with its rooftop views (~€3.50), and the charming marina area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free Faro Municipal Museum or browse the pedestrianized shopping streets. Head to Ilha de Faro — a barrier island beach accessible by free footbridge or cheap ferry. Excellent for a final beach afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Faro's old town — excellent restaurant scene with better value than coastal tourist towns. Try a traditional Algarvian cataplana (copper pot seafood stew) in a local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Faro café near the old town — Portuguese breakfast spread (~€4–5)
meals.lunch: Snack bar near Ilha de Faro beach — grilled sardines on bread with lemon (~€5–7)
meals.dinner: Faro old town restaurant — cataplana de peixe (fish cataplana) shared for two with wine (~€13–16/person)

day_by_day.notes: Faro is underrated by tourists who rush through it to the beach resorts. The old town is genuinely beautiful and almost entirely free to explore. Ilha de Faro is one of the best beaches in the region.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach morning — make the most of the resort's beachfront location. Swim, snorkel, or simply relax and soak up the last of the Algarve sunshine. Take photos and enjoy a slow, peaceful morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping near the resort or in the nearest town. Look for affordable Portuguese gifts: local wine bottles (~€4–8), ginjinha (cherry liqueur), local honey, handmade ceramic tiles (azulejos), or locally made cork products.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the best local restaurant you've discovered during the trip. Splurge slightly on your final night — order a full spread including amêijoas à Bulhão Pato (clams in garlic and white wine) as a starter.

meals.breakfast: Slow resort or local café breakfast — full spread to enjoy the morning (~€5–7)
meals.lunch: Light beach snack — fruit, olives, local bread from supermarket (~€4–5)
meals.dinner: Best local restaurant of the trip — full Portuguese feast with wine (~€18–22/person as a treat)

day_by_day.notes: Pack your bags tonight to make departure day smooth. Keep receipts for any wine or food purchases over €50 if you want to claim VAT refund at the airport (non-EU travelers). Leave a tip for excellent service — 5–10% is appreciated.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy one last pastel de nata and galão at a local café before heading to Faro Airport. Take a final walk along the beach if time allows before departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Faro Airport. Allow extra time for check-in and security. Browse duty-free for any last Portuguese wine or port purchases (often good value at airport duty-free for EU-produced goods).
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Reflect on 13 wonderful days in the Algarve — beaches explored, wines tasted, and memories made on a budget.

meals.breakfast: Final local café — pastel de nata, galão, fresh orange juice (~€3–4)
meals.lunch: Airport café or packed snacks from supermarket (~€5–8)
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary tip: With careful planning, this 13-day Algarve trip can be done for €60–80/day per person including accommodation, meals, transport, and activities. September is the sweet spot — great weather, lower prices, and fewer crowds than peak summer.

trip_options.title: Classic Portugal Algarve Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Faro Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort (approximately 30–45 min drive). Check in, freshen up, and settle into your beachfront room.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely first stroll along the beachfront directly from the resort. Explore the immediate shoreline, dip your toes in the Atlantic, and get oriented with the surroundings. Visit the resort's beach bar for a welcome drink.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed dinner at the resort's restaurant to ease into the trip. Stroll along the promenade after dinner and watch the sunset over the Atlantic.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport meal
meals.lunch: Light snack at Faro Airport or grab a pastel de nata and coffee at a café near the airport before transfer
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort restaurant — try the grilled sea bass (robalo) with local vegetables and a glass of Algarve white wine

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — focus on arrival, settling in, and acclimatizing. Confirm any pre-booked experiences with the resort concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Full beach morning at the resort's beachfront. Swim, snorkel along the shore, or simply relax on a sun lounger. The September sea is still warm (~22°C) and crowds are thinner than peak summer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bike or take a short taxi/Uber to explore the nearby coastal town. Visit local shops, a fish market, and pick up some regional almonds and fig sweets as snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a local seafood restaurant in town for a proper Algarvian dinner experience. Try the cataplana de marisco (seafood stew cooked in a traditional copper pot).

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast — fresh fruit, local cheeses, bread, and coffee
meals.lunch: Beachside snack bar — grilled sardines on bread (sardinhas assadas) and a cold Sagres beer
meals.dinner: Local mid-range seafood restaurant in town — cataplana de marisco for two, house white wine, dessert of Dom Rodrigo (Algarvian almond sweet)

day_by_day.notes: September is ideal beach weather in the Algarve — expect sunny skies and temperatures around 26–28°C. Apply sunscreen generously.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Ponta da Piedade near Lagos — one of the most dramatic coastal rock formations in the Algarve. Hire a local boat tour (~1 hour) to explore the golden limestone arches, grottos, and hidden sea caves up close.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Lagos old town on foot. Walk the historic city walls, visit the Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos), and browse the charming cobblestone streets. Stop at a local café for a bica (espresso) and pastéis.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Lagos at a mid-range restaurant. Try the amêijoas à Bulhão Pato (clams in garlic and white wine) and grilled dourada (sea bream).

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Casual tasca in Lagos — prego sandwich (steak roll) or bifanas with local beer
meals.dinner: A Forja or similar mid-range Lagos restaurant — clams, grilled fish, local Algarve wine, and tarte de amendoa (almond tart) for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Lagos is approximately 20–30 min from most Algarve beachfront resorts. Rent a car for the day or use a taxi/rideshare. Book the boat tour at Ponta da Piedade in advance during September.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting morning at a local Algarve winery. Visit Quinta dos Vales or Adega do Cantor (Sir Cliff Richard's famous estate near Guia/Albufeira area) for a guided vineyard tour and tasting of regional Algarve wines including Negra Mole and Castelão varieties.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the winery, visit the nearby Silves — the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Explore the impressive red sandstone Silves Castle (Castelo de Silves) and the Gothic Cathedral. Wander the riverside town.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Silves or back near the resort. Try the regional pork dishes — the Algarve is known for excellent porco preto (black pork).

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Light cheese, charcuterie, and wine pairing at the winery (often included in tour packages)
meals.dinner: Marisqueira in Silves or resort area — grilled black pork secretos, roasted vegetables, and a bottle of Algarve red wine

day_by_day.notes: Book the winery tour in advance. Quinta dos Vales and Adega do Cantor both offer English-language tours. A rental car is recommended for this day to combine the winery and Silves efficiently.

day_by_day.morning: Beach day at Praia da Marinha — consistently rated one of the most beautiful beaches in Europe. Arrive early to secure a good spot among the dramatic limestone cliffs and turquoise coves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Coastal cliff walk along the Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos (Seven Hanging Valleys Trail) — a stunning 5.7 km cliff-top walk between Praia de Vale Centianes and Praia da Marinha offering breathtaking ocean views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort for a shower and rest, then enjoy dinner at a local restaurant near the resort — a relaxed evening after an active day.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from a local bakery/supermarket — local bread, cheese, Algarvian figs, almonds, and water for the trail
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant near resort — fresh tuna steak (atum) with tomato rice, a local specialty, and a glass of chilled vinho verde

day_by_day.notes: Praia da Marinha is near Lagoa/Carvoeiro. Wear sturdy shoes for the cliff walk and bring plenty of water. The trail is moderately easy but exposed — sun protection is essential.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure — sleep in, enjoy a long resort breakfast, and spend time by the pool or beach. This is a deliberate rest day to maintain a balanced pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Albufeira's old town (Cidade Velha) — explore the whitewashed streets, local art galleries, and the famous fishermen's beach (Praia dos Pescadores). Browse the artisan market for local ceramics and cork products.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop or clifftop bar in Albufeira. Then dinner at a mid-range restaurant in the old town.

meals.breakfast: Extended resort breakfast — take your time and enjoy the beachfront view
meals.lunch: Café in Albufeira old town — tostas mistas (toasted ham and cheese) and fresh-squeezed orange juice
meals.dinner: O Zé or similar Albufeira old town restaurant — açorda de marisco (seafood bread stew) and local wine

day_by_day.notes: Albufeira old town is much quieter in September compared to July/August. Enjoy the more relaxed atmosphere while still experiencing the town's charm.

day_by_day.morning: Second wine tasting experience — visit Herdade dos Grous or Quinta da Tôr near Loulé for a more intimate boutique winery experience. Explore the vineyard, learn about the winemaking process, and taste 4–5 wines including the local Arinto white and Syrah blends.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Loulé — a charming inland Algarvian market town. Visit the covered market (Mercado de Loulé) for local produce, honey, smoked sausages, and handicrafts. Explore the small Moorish castle and old town.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort for a relaxed evening. Enjoy a bottle of wine purchased at the winery on your balcony overlooking the beach.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Winery lunch pairing or a simple meal at a local tasca near Loulé — caldo verde (kale soup) and bread
meals.dinner: In-resort dining or nearby beachfront restaurant — grilled swordfish (espadarte) with lemon and olive oil, salad, and local wine

day_by_day.notes: Loulé market is best visited on Saturday mornings for the full experience — consider adjusting if Day 7 falls on a Saturday. The Loulé Gypsy Market (held every Sunday) is also worth noting.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente — the southwestern tip of Europe. Visit the dramatic Sagres Fortress (Fortaleza de Sagres) perched on the cliff edge, and then drive to Cabo de São Vicente lighthouse for spectacular ocean panoramas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Sagres village and its beautiful beaches — Praia do Martinhal and Praia do Tonel are stunning and typically uncrowded in September. Swim and relax in the wild, windswept Atlantic setting.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Sagres before the drive back — the village has excellent fresh fish restaurants given its active fishing port.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast (early start recommended)
meals.lunch: Sagres seafood restaurant near the harbor — fresh grilled fish of the day (peixe do dia) with salad and local wine
meals.dinner: A Tasca or similar Sagres eatery — percebes (barnacles, a local delicacy), more fresh fish, and a glass of Sagres beer

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is approximately 1–1.5 hours from central Algarve. A rental car is essential. It can be windy at Cabo de São Vicente — bring a light jacket. Start early to make the most of the day.

day_by_day.morning: Full relaxation beach morning at the resort. This mid-trip rest day is intentional. Enjoy water sports offered by the resort — paddleboarding, kayaking, or a jet ski session.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local spa or wellness center near the resort for a massage or treatment. Alternatively, explore a nearby nature reserve or take a stand-up paddleboard lesson on calmer waters.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner cruise along the Algarve coast — many operators run 2-hour sunset boat trips with wine and snacks. Book in advance.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Resort beach bar — light salad, grilled chicken wrap, and fresh fruit juice
meals.dinner: Sunset boat cruise with wine and canapés included, followed by a light late snack at a resort bar if still hungry

day_by_day.notes: Sunset cruise operators include Seafaris Algarve and Dream Wave. The September sunsets (~19:30–20:00) are spectacular. Book the cruise at least 2–3 days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Faro — the Algarve's capital city. Visit the historic walled old town (Cidade Velha), the Gothic Faro Cathedral (Se de Faro) with its rooftop views, and the charming Arco da Vila gateway.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a ferry from Faro to the Ria Formosa Natural Park — a stunning coastal lagoon system. Explore the barrier islands (Ilha Deserta or Ilha da Culatra) with pristine, remote beaches. Swim in calm lagoon waters.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Faro before returning to the resort. Faro has excellent mid-range dining options.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Picnic on Ilha Deserta or eat at the small restaurant on the island — fresh fish and salads
meals.dinner: Faro mid-range restaurant — try the local specialty arroz de lingueirão (razor clam rice) and a glass of Alentejo wine

day_by_day.notes: Ferry departures from Faro pier are frequent. Ilha Deserta has a restaurant (Estaminé) that is worth a visit but can be pricey — book ahead if dining there. Ria Formosa is a UNESCO-listed natural park.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Tavira — one of the most beautiful and authentic towns in the Algarve. Explore the Roman bridge, the Castle of Tavira, the Church of Santa Maria do Castelo, and the charming riverside promenade.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a water taxi from Tavira to Ilha de Tavira — a stunning barrier island beach. September means quieter beaches and warm water. Spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing on this pristine stretch of sand.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Tavira before returning — Tavira is known for excellent traditional Algarvian cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar on Ilha de Tavira — grilled chicken, salad, and cold drinks
meals.dinner: Tavira restaurant (Quatro Aguas area is famous for seafood) — arroz de linguado (sole rice) or grilled whole fish, local wine, and almond dessert

day_by_day.notes: Tavira is in the eastern Algarve — approximately 35–45 min from central Algarve. A rental car is ideal. Water taxis to Ilha de Tavira run regularly in summer/early autumn.

day_by_day.morning: Final wine experience — visit a local wine shop or deli in the resort area for a curated tasting session of Algarve, Alentejo, and Douro wines side by side. Purchase bottles to bring home (check airline liquid allowances).
day_by_day.afternoon: Last proper beach afternoon at the resort's beachfront. Take a final swim, enjoy the sun, and soak in the Algarve atmosphere. Collect shells, take photos, and reflect on the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Special farewell dinner at the best mid-range restaurant you've discovered during the trip, or try somewhere new — splurge slightly for a memorable final dinner.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Light lunch at resort beach bar — fresh salad, seafood skewers, and a glass of chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Celebratory farewell dinner — choose your favorite dish from the trip, order a special bottle of wine (perhaps a Quinta dos Vales reserve), and finish with a medronho (local firewater) digestif

day_by_day.notes: Begin packing this evening. Keep wine purchases in checked luggage (bottles well-wrapped). Confirm departure transfer for the following day.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy one last resort breakfast with ocean views. Take a brief final walk along the beach. Check out of the resort (standard checkout is usually 11:00 — request late checkout if your flight allows).
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Faro Airport. If time allows before transfer, stop at a local supermarket to pick up last-minute Portuguese souvenirs — local honey, fleur de sel sea salt, canned fish (conservas), almond sweets, and a bottle of ginjinha or medronho.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days of beaches, wine, seafood, and Algarvian culture.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — make it a good one
meals.lunch: Light snack at Faro Airport — pastel de nata and a final bica (espresso) before boarding
meals.dinner: In-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2 hours before flight departure for airport check-in and security. Faro Airport is small but can get busy. Confirm your LH flight departure time and arrange transfer accordingly. Safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning coastlines along the cliffside trail connecting Praia da Marinha to Benagil. Descend to hidden grottos, golden coves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters for a swim. The dramatic limestone rock formations make this an unmissable beach experience.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the world's most beautiful sea caves, accessible only by water. A guided kayak tour takes you through hidden sea arches, natural tunnels, and secluded beaches inaccessible by foot. An unforgettable blend of adventure and natural beauty.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour
experiences.description: Visit local Algarvian wineries in the Lagos and Portimão hinterland, sampling indigenous grape varieties like Negra Mole and Crato Branco. Enjoy guided cellar tours, barrel tastings, and food pairings with regional cheeses and charcuterie. A wonderful way to discover the lesser-known wines of southern Portugal.

experiences.name: Sagres Sunset & Ponta de Sagres Fortress Visit
experiences.description: Journey to the dramatic southwestern tip of Europe at Cabo de São Vicente and the historic Sagres Fortress, where Henry the Navigator once planned his great voyages of discovery. Watch the sun dip into the Atlantic from the windswept cliffs, then enjoy local wine and petiscos at a nearby tavern in Sagres village.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Faro Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from Faro Airport to Aegean Bliss Resort (approx. 45–60 min). Settle into your beachfront suite, enjoy a welcome amenity and champagne on arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private resort orientation and leisure time. Explore the beachfront grounds, take a refreshing dip in the sea or the infinity pool, and decompress after the flight. Optional: book a 60-minute couples' massage at the resort spa to ease travel fatigue.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's beachfront bar, watching the golden Algarve light fade over the Atlantic. Dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or pre-arrival)
meals.lunch: Light welcome lunch at the resort's poolside bistro upon arrival — grilled sea bass, fresh salads, and chilled Vinho Verde
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's signature restaurant: tasting menu featuring Cataplana de Marisco (traditional Algarvian seafood stew), paired with a curated selection of Alentejo whites and reds

day_by_day.notes: Ensure private transfer is pre-booked. Request early check-in if possible. Keep Day 1 relaxed to recover from travel. Confirm spa appointments in advance for the following days.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the resort followed by a guided Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim. A private guide leads you along the dramatic cliffside trail connecting Praia da Marinha — one of the Algarve's most celebrated coastlines — with stunning views of golden limestone arches, hidden coves, and turquoise waters. Swim in secluded sea grottos accessible only on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a light lunch. Spend the afternoon at leisure on the private beach: sunbathe on premium loungers, enjoy water sports (paddleboarding or snorkeling equipment provided by resort), or book an in-pool cabana session.
day_by_day.evening: Pre-dinner drinks at a clifftop wine bar in nearby Carvoeiro village. Dinner at a renowned local restaurant specializing in contemporary Portuguese cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Full Portuguese breakfast at the resort: fresh pastries, local cheeses, charcuterie, eggs, freshly squeezed orange juice, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort beach club: grilled octopus salad, Algarvian gazpacho, and a chilled glass of Rosé from the Algarve
meals.dinner: Dinner at Bon Bon Restaurant (Carvoeiro) — one of the Algarve's Michelin-starred gems, offering a creative tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable hiking shoes and bring reef-safe sunscreen and swimwear for the coastal hike. Book Bon Bon well in advance as it fills up quickly. Private transfer to and from Carvoeiro recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Private Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour. Depart by private vehicle to Praia de Benagil (approx. 20 min from resort). A certified guide leads an exclusive small-group (or solo couple) kayak tour through the world-famous Benagil Cave — a cathedral-like sea cave with a natural skylight. Paddle through arches, sea stacks, and hidden beaches inaccessible by land.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort. Enjoy a premium spa treatment: choose from a Portuguese-inspired scrub using local sea salt and almond oil, or a deep-tissue massage. Relax in the hammam and sauna facilities.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset aperitivo on your private suite terrace with a bottle of chilled Alvarinho. Dinner at an upscale seafood restaurant in Portimão.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast delivered to your suite terrace: smoked salmon, avocado toast, artisan pastries, fresh fruit, and cold-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Post-kayak light lunch at a clifftop café near Benagil: grilled sardines, local bread, and a glass of crisp Loureiro white wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Vista (Portimão) — a cliffside fine-dining restaurant with panoramic ocean views, specializing in premium seafood and Portuguese contemporary cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Kayak tour requires moderate fitness. Life jackets and all equipment provided. Book the exclusive private kayak tour option for the most intimate experience. Check tide schedules — morning departures offer the calmest conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour — Part 1. Private chauffeured tour departs to the Lagos and Portimão hinterland. Visit the first winery (e.g., Adega do Cantor or Quinta dos Vales), where a master sommelier guides you through the estate vineyards, explains indigenous Algarvian grape varieties (Negra Mole, Crato Branco, Síria), and hosts a private barrel-room tasting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the vineyard tour to a second estate. Enjoy a guided tasting of premium reserve wines paired with a curated cheese and charcuterie board. Explore the olive groves and learn about the estate's production of extra-virgin olive oil — a complementary Algarvian luxury product.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Unwind with a sunset swim. Dinner at the resort's wine-focused restaurant, where the sommelier presents a special Algarvian wine flight to complement the day's discoveries.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at the resort's main dining room: full selection of hot and cold items, freshly baked breads, local honey, and regional jams
meals.lunch: Winery estate lunch: a curated farm-to-table spread of local meats, cheeses, olives, and seasonal vegetables paired with estate wines — served al fresco in the vineyard
meals.dinner: Resort wine dinner: five-course menu with Algarvian wine flight pairing — featuring dishes like black pork secreto, salt cod à Brás, and almond tart with fig compote

day_by_day.notes: Wear light, breathable clothing suitable for vineyard walking. Bring a hat and sunscreen. The sommelier can arrange to ship selected wine bottles to your home country. Confirm wine tour booking 48 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely start. Morning yoga class on the resort's clifftop terrace at sunrise (optional, bookable through the resort's wellness program). Followed by a slow breakfast and a stroll along the private beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private boat charter from a nearby marina (e.g., Portimão or Lagos). Cruise along the Algarve's dramatic coastline aboard a luxury yacht: pass by Praia da Marinha, the Benagil Cave from the sea, Arco Natural, and Ponta da Piedade. Snorkeling stop at a pristine cove. Champagne and canapés served on deck.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset return to marina. Freshen up at the resort. Dinner in Lagos old town at a premium restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Healthy resort breakfast: açaí bowls, granola, Greek yogurt, tropical fruits, green juices, and specialty teas
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic served on the yacht deck: smoked fish, artisan bread, local cheeses, seasonal fruit, and a bottle of chilled Alvarinho Soalheiro
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Adega da Marina (Lagos) or a comparable premium Lagos waterfront restaurant — grilled tiger prawns, lobster bisque, and local Douro red wine

day_by_day.notes: Book the private yacht charter at least 3 days in advance. Half-day or full-day options available — full-day recommended for maximum coastline exploration. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a light layer for sea breeze, and a camera.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Lagos on foot. Private guided walking tour of Lagos historic center: visit the 15th-century Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos), the Igreja de Santo António with its stunning gilded Baroque interior, the medieval city walls, and the vibrant Praça Gil Eanes. Browse local artisan boutiques for ceramics, cork goods, and handmade jewelry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Ponta da Piedade — Lagos's most iconic geological landmark. Walk the clifftop trail and descend to the sea-level grottos by private boat. Explore the golden limestone arches, sea stacks, and hidden caves. Return to the resort for a relaxing afternoon by the pool.
day_by_day.evening: Cocktail hour at the resort bar. Dinner at an acclaimed restaurant in the Algarve hinterland for a rustic-luxury dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast: hot buffet with eggs cooked to order, smoked meats, pastries, and fresh-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Lunch at a charming Lagos café: petiscos (Portuguese tapas) — chouriço assado, gambas al ajillo, bifanas, and local wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Laranjeira (Lagos) or equivalent — tasting menu with regional Algarvian specialties and a curated wine pairing from the Alentejo and Algarve

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Lagos tour and the Ponta da Piedade cliff trail. The boat tour at Ponta da Piedade is typically 30–45 minutes — book through the resort concierge. September light is spectacular for photography at golden hour.

day_by_day.morning: Full rest and resort indulgence day. Sleep in and enjoy a late in-room breakfast. Morning at leisure: read by the pool, enjoy a private stretch session with the resort's personal trainer, or book a rejuvenating facial at the spa.
day_by_day.afternoon: Resort spa afternoon: full body wrap using local carob and almond extracts, followed by a hydrotherapy circuit (jacuzzi, contrast pools, steam room). Optional: private tennis or padel court session on resort facilities.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset champagne tasting curated by the resort sommelier — a flight of premium Champagne and Crémant paired with oysters and caviar blinis on your suite terrace. Dinner at the resort's beachfront fine-dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent in-room brunch: eggs Benedict, smoked salmon bagels, fresh pastries, fruit platters, Bellinis, and specialty coffee — served on the private terrace
meals.lunch: Light poolside snack: chilled gazpacho, bruschetta, and a glass of rosé
meals.dinner: Beachfront tasting menu at the resort's signature restaurant: seven-course menu with wine pairing — highlights include Algarve red shrimp tartare, black pork tenderloin, and a deconstructed Dom Rodrigo (traditional almond and egg dessert)

day_by_day.notes: This is a designated rest and recovery day — essential for a 13-day trip. Encourage guests to fully utilize spa and wellness amenities. Pre-book the sommelier champagne tasting experience through the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Sagres Sunset & Ponta de Sagres Fortress Visit — morning departure. Private chauffeured drive to Sagres (approx. 1 hour from resort). Visit the historic Fortaleza de Sagres — the dramatic clifftop fortress from which Henry the Navigator launched Portugal's Age of Discovery. Explore the windswept promontory, the enigmatic Rosa dos Ventos (compass rose), and the Chapel of Our Lady of Grace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Cabo de São Vicente — the southwesternmost point of continental Europe. Stand at the edge of the known world on the dramatic 75-meter-high cliffs. Visit the iconic lighthouse. Explore the small artisan market at the cape for local crafts. Optional: short hike along the clifftop trail with Atlantic panoramas.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the legendary Cabo de São Vicente sunset — one of the most spectacular in Europe, drawing visitors from across the continent. Return to resort. Late dinner at a premium Sagres or Lagos restaurant, or back at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure: continental spread with pastries, cold cuts, cheeses, and strong espresso
meals.lunch: Lunch in Sagres village at a quality seafood restaurant: grilled dourada (sea bream), barnacles (percebes), and chilled Alvarinho
meals.dinner: Dinner at a premium restaurant in Vila do Bispo or Lagos on the return journey — or resort dinner upon return: cataplana de peixe (fish cataplana) and Algarvian desserts

day_by_day.notes: Bring a warm layer — the wind at Cabo de São Vicente and Sagres can be strong even in September. Sunset time in mid-September is approximately 19:45–20:00. This is a full-day excursion — plan for a 7–8 hour day including travel. Bring a camera for the fortress and sunset.

day_by_day.morning: Private surf lesson or stand-up paddleboard session on the resort's beach. A certified instructor provides a 90-minute private session tailored to your level. September offers excellent Atlantic swells and warm water temperatures (approx. 22–24°C). Alternatively, a guided snorkeling tour of the nearby rocky reefs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit to Silves — the medieval Moorish capital of the Algarve. Private guided tour of the impressive red sandstone Castelo de Silves, the Gothic Cathedral, and the charming riverside town. Browse local ceramic and cork artisan shops. Visit a local almond and carob farm.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. Sunset cocktails. Dinner in Silves or at a nearby quinta (estate) for a farm-to-table dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast: full hot and cold buffet with made-to-order omelets, smoked fish, and freshly baked bread
meals.lunch: Lunch in Silves at Restaurante Marisqueira Rui or equivalent — whole grilled lobster, tiger prawns, and a bottle of chilled white wine from the Alentejo
meals.dinner: Dinner at Quinta do Freixo or a comparable Silves hinterland estate — rustic-luxury menu: black pork cheeks, roasted vegetables, and Algarvian wines in a candlelit quinta setting

day_by_day.notes: Silves is approximately 30–40 minutes from the resort. The castle is best visited in the morning before crowds arrive. September is harvest season — ask locally about any wine or orange harvest events happening nearby.

day_by_day.morning: Second Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour — focusing on a different wine region. Private chauffeured tour to Tavira or the eastern Algarve hinterland to visit a boutique winery (e.g., Quinta da Tôr or Quinta do Barranco Longo). Private tasting of premium reserve and aged wines with the winemaker. Tour of the cellars and fermentation facilities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Tavira — one of the Algarve's most elegant and historic towns. Stroll across the Roman bridge, visit the hilltop castle and its gardens, and explore the mosaic-tiled churches and whitewashed townhouses. Browse Tavira's upscale boutiques and gourmet food shops for local preserves, wines, and ceramics.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks at a rooftop bar in Tavira overlooking the Gilão River. Dinner at a premium Tavira restaurant before private transfer back to resort.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast: freshly baked croissants, smoked ham, local cheeses, seasonal fruit, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Winery estate lunch: paired tasting menu with estate wines — five courses featuring local produce including Algarvian almonds, figs, and black pork
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante O Pátio (Tavira) or equivalent — creative Portuguese cuisine with eastern Algarve influences: tuna tataki, salt cod with chickpeas, and a curated wine list

day_by_day.notes: Tavira is approximately 1 hour east of the resort — plan for an early departure. The eastern Algarve has a distinctly different character from the western coast — more traditional and less touristic. September is an excellent time as summer crowds have thinned.

day_by_day.morning: Private golf experience at one of the Algarve's world-class golf courses (e.g., Penina Golf Resort, Monte Rei, or Amendoeira Golf Resort). A private caddie and optional PGA instructor accompany you for a full 18-hole round on a championship course set against stunning Algarvian scenery. Alternatively, for non-golfers: a private horseback riding tour along the beach and coastal trails.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to resort. Indulge in a premium spa treatment: hot stone massage or a couples' ritual using local carob, almond, and citrus extracts. Afternoon tea served in the resort lounge.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset sailing trip from the nearest marina — a 2-hour sunset cruise aboard a luxury catamaran with a dedicated crew, champagne, and canapés. Return to resort for a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early golf breakfast at the resort: high-energy spread with eggs, smoked salmon, whole grain breads, fresh juices, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Clubhouse lunch at the golf resort: club sandwich, Caesar salad, and a glass of chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Late resort dinner: à la carte menu featuring premium Iberian black pork secreto, roasted sea bass with clams, and a bottle of Pêra-Manca Branco (one of Portugal's finest whites)

day_by_day.notes: Book golf tee times at least one week in advance — September is still peak season for golf in the Algarve. Rental clubs available at all major courses. The sunset sailing trip should be booked through the resort concierge — departure typically at 18:30.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach morning — make the most of the Algarve's stunning coastline. Private beach butler service with premium loungers, cold towels, and chilled beverages. Morning swim, paddleboarding, or simply reading in the sun. Optional: final snorkeling excursion to a nearby rocky reef with the resort's water sports team.
day_by_day.afternoon: Farewell spa ritual: a 2-hour premium couples' spa journey — full-body exfoliation, aromatherapy massage, and a private jacuzzi session overlooking the sea. Followed by a final stroll along the cliffside promenade near the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell gala dinner — the resort's most exclusive dining experience. Reserve the private dining room or a candle-lit table on the beach. Chef's special tasting menu celebrating the flavors of the Algarve, paired with a prestige wine selection chosen by the head sommelier.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely full resort breakfast: everything on the menu — a final celebration of Portuguese morning flavors
meals.lunch: Beachside light lunch: chilled seafood platter (oysters, clams, prawns), crusty bread with garlic butter, and a bottle of Vinho Verde
meals.dinner: Private farewell dinner: eight-course chef's tasting menu — Algarve red shrimp, barnacles, black pork, local cheeses, Dom Rodrigo dessert, and a premium wine pairing including a vintage Port to close the evening

day_by_day.notes: Book the private beach or private dining room for the farewell dinner well in advance. Consider purchasing a curated wine selection from the resort sommelier to take home. Pack non-essential luggage tonight to ease the morning departure.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure. Enjoy a last sunrise walk along the beach. Leisurely checkout breakfast. Resort concierge arranges private luxury transfer to Faro Airport. Say farewell to the Algarve.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer to Faro Airport. Departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure / in-transit.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast: full spread with all favorites — pastries, eggs, smoked fish, fresh juices, and a final espresso with a view of the Atlantic
meals.lunch: Light airport lunch or in-flight dining
meals.dinner: In-flight or post-arrival

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time and private transfer booking the evening before. Allow at least 2.5 hours before departure for the transfer and airport procedures. Request a late checkout if the flight allows — many luxury resorts accommodate this. Ensure all purchased wines and local products are properly packed for travel.
